problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. The available containers are:

* Container 1: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue 144 credits
* Container 2: volume 21 cubic meters, revenue 183 credits
* Container 3: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue 241 credits
* Container 4: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue 86 credits
* Container 5: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue 19 credits
* Container 6: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue 218 credits
* Container 7: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue 256 credits
* Container 8: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue 282 credits
* Container 9: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue 124 credits
* Container 10: volume 19 cubic meters, revenue 93 credits
* Container 11: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue 112 credits
* Container 12: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue 134 credits
* Container 13: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue 148 credits
* Container 14: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue 106 credits
* Container 15: volume 37 cubic meters, revenue 176 credits
* Container 16: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue 42 credits
* Container 17: volume 25 cubic meters, revenue 109 credits
* Container 18: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue 115 credits
* Container 19: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue 116 credits
* Container 20: volume 25 cubic meters, revenue 93 credits
* Container 21: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue 164 credits
* Container 22: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue 50 credits
* Container 23: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue 58 credits
* Container 24: volume 50 cubic meters, revenue 167 credits
* Container 25: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue 24 credits
* Container 26: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue 188 credits

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 492 cubic meters. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
